question.problem:
The number $y(t)$ of people in a closed community who have been infected with a virus follows the logistic growth model

$$
{y}^{′}=2400y-3{y}^{2},\,y(0)=12,
$$

where $t$ is the time, in days, since the observations began. According to this model, what is the maximum possible number of infected people?

The maximum possible number of infected people is
{{field-1}}.
question.worked_solution:
A logistic growth equation has the form

$$
{y}^{′}=ky(a-y),
$$

where $k>0$ is a constant of proportionality, and $a>y$ is the carrying capacity. 

The carrying capacity $a$ represents the maximum possible number of people who will be infected. A diagram showing a typical logistic growth curve is shown below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14157279/assets/d8133f1c4203903bac606bbae61c73717e2ba2dc15a97a77f48eaaeaf4736d06.png)

First, let's rewrite the right-hand side of the given equation so that it matches the form above:

$$
\begin{aligned}{y}^{′} & =2400y-3{y}^{2} \\  & =3y(800-y)\end{aligned}
$$

From here, we see that $a=800.$ Hence, the carrying capacity is $800,$ and we conclude that the maximum possible number of infected people is $800.$
